note: Three family campgrounds off the main park road. The wooded 300 campground sits on a bluff above Little Falls Lake, with sites 313-319 and 352-360 on the lake side; the newer 100 campground is open with little shade and takes the largest rigs; the 200 campground lies between them. The beach and nature center are a short walk west of the 300 loop. --Claude

flags: WATERFRONT: lakeview KEPT (checked hard). Only the 300 campground touches the lake: the DNR map draws Little Falls Lake along its NW edge beside sites 313-319 and 352-360 (nightly state-park sites). On Esri imagery (zoom 18 around 45.0148,-92.6928) the loop is under continuous canopy and its lake-side edge sits ~60-90 m from the shore, atop the wooded bluff the DNR mentions ('you may encounter steep bluffs') - a climb-down, not an apron, so not lakefront. A view rests on the official per-site map putting those sites at the lake edge; no official campsite photo was readable (GoingToCamp refuses). The 100 and 200 campgrounds are 400 m+ from any water (not waterfront).

PIN: stored 45.0127,-92.6926 is on the park road ~165 m south of the 300 loop's centre (~45.0141,-92.6918) - kept. The 200 loop centre is ~45.0143,-92.6844 (~580 m east of the 300) and the 100 loop ~45.0150,-92.6792 (~990 m east); all three leave the one main park road behind the single entrance and are run as one campground ('Willow River's campground') - not proposed as a split.
